To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the activity of STN neurons under propofol is characterized by decreased firing rate and increased bursting activity, 2) parametric and non-parametric approaches give different results in the analysis of neuronal activity and 3) the random forest trees algorithm is more suitable for the analysis of spike trains compared to generalised line models
the neuronal activity in STN of PD patients under propofol anesthesia differs from the awake state.
the firing rate and bursting activity are the most informative neuronal activity parameters in STN of patients with Parkinson's disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods to analyse neuronal activity in human patients and the comparison of the results obtained by parametric and non-parametric methods.

the development of methods for the analysis of single neuron activity in the human brain and their application to the study of the changes of the activity in the STN of Parkinsonian patients under local and general anaesthesia.
the analysis of single neuron activity in human STN under different conditions, and the results obtained are of interest for the development of a reliable and robust classification algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a significant difference in neuronal activity in STN of Parkinsonian patients under anaesthesia compared with the awake state.
the most important parameters of neuronal activity are the ones that are most sensitive to anaesthesia and are also the most important for classification of the activity.
the most important features for classification of neuronal activity are firing rate and burstiness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analysis of neuronal activity under propofol is feasible using a variety of approaches.
the analysis of the neuronal activity of patients with PD under anaesthesia is a complicated task.
the analysis of the neuronal activity of STN patients in anaesthesia should be performed with the help of a nonparametric classification method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the analysis method should depend on the purpose of the analysis.
the choice of a classification algorithm should be based not only on the accuracy, but also on the interpretation of the classification results.
the choice of a particular approach for the analysis of single unit activity is crucial for the correct interpretation of results.
